newsitem.title: GERMANY: Siemens unit pressured by chip pricing.
newsitem.headline: Siemens unit pressured by chip pricing.

text.p: The semiconductor unit of Siemens AG, while predicting strong long-term growth, said on Thursday falling chip prices would weigh on profit in 1996/97.
"Naturally we have a challenge this year," said semiconductor sales chief Peter Fischl at a news conference.
"It all depends on the price dynamic. We have work to do but we are optimistic we will be in the black for this year."

The unit, the world's 12th largest chip maker, reported 603 million marks in pretax profit in the year that ended September 30. But BHF Bank in Frankfurt forecasted a drop of about 66 percent to around 200 million marks this year.
Siemens said it expected improvements in productivity and manufacturing, but admitted these gains would not offset the impact of price declines.
At the same time, the unit's costs were expected to continue rising. Capital investment climbed 71 percent in 1995/96 to 2.2 billion marks, while the payroll rose 22 percent to 19,316 workers.

Prospects were brighter in the long term, as Siemens forecasted 26 percent average annual sales growth over the next five years. It expected prices to stabilise next year as the Internet, expanding corporate networks, mobile and wireless communications drove demand for semiconductors.
The unit said it was expanding manufacturing capacity in Asia and North America and planned strategic partnerships to support its growth targets.
